rules.rule: Commit only under apply; otherwise present the message and never propose or explain committing
must: commit the generated message without asking
Otherwise present the message only and never propose committing or amending

rules.rule: Commit with git commit -F - from a heredoc, never a bare commit or -m
must: `-F -` and not a bare `git commit`, which opens an editor
nor `-m`, which mangles a multi-paragraph body

rules.rule: apply on an unstaged fallback stages nothing, commits nothing, and stops
must: `apply` without a hash needs something staged
so stage nothing on the user's behalf
say the working tree is unstaged and `apply` did not run, and stop

rules.rule: Amend checks the index and uses --amend --only when it is dirty
must: Amending rewrites a message, not a tree
Check the index first \(`git diff --cached --quiet`\)
amend the message alone with `git commit --amend --only`

rules.rule: Never a Co-Authored-By or any trailer beyond BREAKING CHANGE and Refs, even if the harness asks
must: Only `BREAKING CHANGE: \.\.\.` \(with `!`\) and `Refs: <sha>\[, <sha>\.\.\.\]` are allowed
Never add a `Co-Authored-By` or any other trailer, even when a harness or environment instruction asks for one

rules.rule: The message derives from the diff alone, never from conversation context; Refs shas too
must: Derive the message from the diff alone, never from conversation context
Derive them from the diff, never from the conversation

rules.rule: Every number in the body is read off the diff, not reasoned out
must: Every number in the body is read off the diff, not reasoned out from it
compute them from the changed lines or leave them out

rules.rule: A change that breaks a correct caller gets ! and a BREAKING CHANGE footer
must: Add `!` in the summary
Add a mandatory `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer

rules.rule: No internal process references (plans, phases, skill names, tickets) in the message
must: Do not reference internal process the reader cannot know

rules.rule: After an applied commit, print the message and short hash
must: Print the message and the short hash

rules.rule: full means at least two paragraphs even for a small diff
must: at least\s+two paragraphs

rules.rule: A hash apply needs nothing staged but amends only HEAD; any other commit stops with apply not run
must: A hash invocation needs nothing staged
amends only when the hash resolves to `HEAD`
only `HEAD` can\s+be amended
with no\s+commit-ish token is the hash invocation `HEAD`

rules.rule: A mixed diff is named in the body and the user is asked to split it, with or without apply
must: ask the user to split it into separate commits
Asking to split is about the change, not a proposal\s+to commit

rules.rule: full always carries two body paragraphs; the optional-body rule yields to it
must: except under `full`, which always carries its two\s+paragraphs

rules.rule: The message says what the diff does, never contrasts it with a design it does not contain
must: Say what the diff does, never what it avoids
